items.title: Emile Barnes Interview, 1962-01-03
items.q: Well, after I got to Kelly, well I was probably stuck with Kelly... I had a bar playing band... That band would change so much.

ctx.x: Now, how did he sound with Chris Kelly? Because you know, he plays a lot of sweet clarinet, doesn't he? Well... He does a lot of readings, doesn't he? He's a musician.

I'll tell you that. You see, Kelly was a hard son. And he took the good man to play the night. George played with him. Before I got angry with him, walked up the music stand. What happened? He got George.

items.title: Emile Barnes Interview, 1960-07-29
items.q: when I was with you, with Kelley's band. That was a bunch of men that actually knew each other.

ctx.x: Did they play a lot of clarinet in the low register?

No. I don't remember anybody playing clarinet in the low register until I started playing. I never, none of nobody else in the register and above the register. In fact, I'll tell you about myself, I'm not much above the register. It's good enough with a full orchestra, you know, the bigger band. But whether you take, for instance, you take a short band, it's disagreeable. You understand? Not to get way up, man. You can go maybe a portion of it, but you shouldn't go up as you, as you ought to, with a small band.…
You know, I was wondering, how soft would they entertain in those old days? Would they always play the last chorus real loud or would they play it soft or what?

items.title: Emile Barnes Interview, 1962-02-07
items.q: And that was all we'd be behind shoving them and he'd be going with it.

ctx.x: Getting back a bit to Chris Kelly, did Chris ever play with a mute?
Mute? Yeah, did he use mute? Oh, he, Chris had, Chris had, uh, mute the Vulcan.
